validator: draft 1 passes (no problems, soft or warnings); the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named up front in plain words (mean = area ÷ length; RMS = square, mean, root; sine RMS = peak ÷ √2) and built from what Dan has: lesson 8's i = 3t² and its 8 C, the bars and the reverse rule, lesson 9's mean effective pressure as area ÷ width, P = I²R from his trade and Pythagoras from Geometry fundamentals.

The brief's picture is there and its why needs no trigonometry: the squared sine wave's hump, moved a quarter cycle along and turned over, fills the dip, because height² + sideways² = peak² on the circle at every moment. Hand-checked: sin² + cos² gives the square a quarter cycle on as 100 − the square now, so the fold is exact.

Every misconception the brief names has a DO screen with its own slip: the average of the end values (1, 2), the whole-cycle mean of zero (4), half the peak as the sine's mean (4), the plain mean as RMS (6, 8, 12), the forgotten root (6), peak ÷ 2 for peak ÷ √2 (8), the form factor upside down (10), dividing to get the peak (11), the sine rule used on a ramp (12).

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10) and end on two mixed puzzles (11, 12); the brief's three pictures (sine squared folding, ramp by the power rule, bar count for the half-cycle mean and form factor) are all there.
fix: Causal step skipped: 'the steady current that heats the same is the one whose square equals the mean of the squared current' jumps a step. Show it: at each moment the heater takes i²R; over a cycle its mean power is (mean of i²) × R; a steady I gives I²R; the R is the same on both sides, so equal heating needs I² = mean of i². Also write the changing current's power as i²R, not I²R.

Causal step skipped: 'Any ramp ... its square's mean is A² ÷ 3' is asserted, though the brief says the power rule gives it. Work it: i = A × t ÷ T, square A² × t² ÷ T², reverse rule A² × t³ ÷ (3T²), which at T is A² × T ÷ 3; divide by the length T.
Causal step skipped: the ramp's mean 'its triangle's 6 C' needs the triangle: half of 2 s × 6 A.
Causal step skipped: why the squared sine wave repeats every half cycle. Add the clause: the backward half squares to the same humps, because a minus squared is a plus.

False absolute: 'The 0.707 belongs to the sine wave only' is untrue (a current switched between 10 A and 0 for equal times also has RMS 7.07 A). Say 0.707 is the sine wave's figure and other shapes usually give others, so square, mean and root.
False absolute: 'right only on a straight line' for the average of the ends. Some curves also agree. Say it is right on a straight line but not in general, as the 3t² curve shows.
False absolute in the rule of thumb: the square wave's RMS equals its mean and its peak, so 'lies between' needs 'at or between'.

Brief shows the effect without the cause: whatAmILookingAt must say why the hump fits the dip (a quarter cycle on, the square is 100 minus the square now), and the explain should say the hump moves a quarter cycle along and turns over, as the picture does.
whatAmILookingAt does not say where each half-cycle bar takes its height; name it as the current at the bar's middle, as lessons 8 and 9 did, so 6.53 and 6.41 can be reproduced.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these nine fixes; nothing else needs to change.
